neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were part of an unlawful assembly, assaulted the victim and his brother at a bus stand due to political animosity. The victim sustained grievous injuries and later died in the hospital. The prosecution presented evidence from multiple witnesses, including the victim's brother, who described the incident and the weapons used. The victim's brother was examined by a doctor who found multiple incised wounds on him. The deceased's body was subjected to a post-mortem, which revealed 58 injuries, most of which were incised and cutting wounds. The accused were charged with offenses under Sections 147, 148, 307, 324, and 302 of the IPC. The trial court acquitted all accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal of four accused, finding the trial court's decision to be perverse. The High Court endorsed the spontaneity of the FIR and found the prosecution's story to be supported by the evidence of multiple witnesses.

quotes.text: The Trial Court acquitted all the seven accused. On appeal, the High Court held that the judgment of the trial court was perverse and accordingly reversed the acquittal of four accused (the appellants), who were convicted under Section 302 r/w Section 34 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment, whereas the acquittal of other three accused was maintained.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused persons belonged to the Bhartiya Janta Party and that due to political animosity, they formed an unlawful assembly and assaulted PW-1 and his brother with weapons, resulting in the brother's death. The prosecution story was fully supported by the evidence of PW-2 and two independent witnesses (PWs 3 and 4).

quotes.text: According to the prosecution, the accused persons belonged to the Bhartiya Janta Party whereas PW-1 and his brother were workers of the Congress Party, and that on account of political animosity, the accused persons formed themselves into an unlawful assembly and assaulted PW-1 and his brother with sword, axe and knife, when they just got out of a bus at the bus stand.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the facts of the case did not justify interference by the High Court in an appeal against acquittal. They contended that the Trial Court's findings were not perverse and that the prosecution story was not credible, with doubts about the presence and reliability of the witnesses.

quotes.text: It was contended by the appellants that the facts of the case did not justify interference by the High Court in an appeal against acquittal.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the High Court should not interfere in an appeal against acquittal save in exceptional cases, and that interference is called for only if the findings of the Trial Court are not borne out by the evidence and are perverse.

quotes.text: The High Court should not interfere in an appeal against acquittal save in exceptional cases, and that interference in such an appeal is called for, only if the findings of the Trial Court is not borne out by the evidence and is perverse.
